archetype.name: Title Contender (defense-first, Wembanyama-centered)
archetype.definition: A team with the league's best Net Rtg, a top-two defense and a top-five offense, built around the best center on the site and coming off a 62-win, 13-playoff-win season.

report.headline: The margin backs every win; the real question is health, not luck.
report.take:
San Antonio is the best team in the league by the measure that predicts best. Its 12.1 Net Rtg ranks first, its scoring margin of 11.94 a game ranks first, and the 14-3 record is exactly what that margin implies. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0 and winsByDifferential is 14. None of this rests on close-game luck. The site ranks the Spurs only fourth, and the D+ frontcourt grade is the likeliest drag, but the scoreboard says contender. It also matches last season's 62-20, a 1st-place site finish and 13 playoff wins, so this is not a team arriving early. It is a team that got better at the thing it already did well.

The engine is the defense, and the defense starts at the rim. Opponents shoot 60% within four feet, second in the league and well under the 65.3% league mark. The Spurs hold opponents to a 50.8 eFG %, third best, and finish possessions with a 76.0 DRB %, fourth best. The DRtg of 106.7 is a sharp step down from last season's 111.3, which already ranked third. Victor Wembanyama is the reason. He is first of 92 on the center tab with a 16.2 BPM, 508 points on a 36.0 USG % at 62.9 TS %, and a 45.7 On-Off. The offense is more ordinary than its 118.8 ORtg suggests. It ranks fourth mostly because it protects the ball, with a 11.4 TOV % that is second in the league, and because it crashes the glass. The shooting itself is middling: 3P % is 33.7 (24th), and TS % is down from 59.5 last year to 57.6.

The numbers hide two things, one encouraging and one less so. The encouraging one: opponents are hitting 36.8% from three, 24th in the league, despite how little the Spurs give up inside. Some of that is noise, and if it settles toward the 35.4 league average, an already elite defense gets better. The Spurs' own 33.7% from three sits well below last year's 35.9 and should also drift back up. The less encouraging one is how much rides on a single body. Wembanyama is listed Day-To-Day. The minutes behind him are ugly: Luke Kornet's On-Off is -38.4 and Carter Bryant's is -33.4. In the backcourt, Dylan Harper is Out, carrying a 24.5 On-Off, and De'Aaron Fox, at 24.2, is Day-To-Day.

The direction is up. October went 4-2 with 110.17 allowed a game. November went 10-1 at 102.73 allowed, including a 12-game winning streak. Over the last five games, they allowed 6.35 fewer points a game than their season mark. If the core stays upright, this is a 60-win team with the inside track to the West's top seed. If it doesn't, the drop-off is steeper than the record implies.

strengths.title: Rim protection drives a top-two defense
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 60% at the rim, second in the league, and the Spurs hold them to a 50.8 eFG %. The DRtg of 106.7 ranks second and improves on last year's third-ranked 111.3. With Wembanyama behind it, this is structural rather than a hot streak. Opponents' high 3P % suggests the true level may be even better.

strengths.title: A margin that fully earns the record
strengths.body: A 12.1 Net Rtg leads the league, and the point differential of 203 implies exactly 14 wins. W vs Pt Diff is 0. Close-game luck explains none of the start, which is why the record should hold up better than most hot starts. Their one-point win over Dallas is the exception, not the pattern.

strengths.title: Possession control at both ends
strengths.body: A 11.4 TOV % ranks second, and the Spurs grab 52.8% of all rebounds, fourth in the league. They also lead the league in RPG. That combination lets an offense with below-average shooting still post a fourth-ranked ORtg. It repeats last season's profile, so it should last.

concerns.title: Everything runs through one center
concerns.body: Wembanyama's 45.7 On-Off is the whole frontcourt story, and he is listed Day-To-Day. The non-Wembanyama frontcourt minutes are a real problem: Kornet sits at -38.4 and Bryant at -33.4. That is why the group grades D+ even with the top center on the site. Any extended absence would expose a thin frontcourt fast.

concerns.title: Backcourt depth being tested
concerns.body: The A+ backcourt is thinning. Harper, fifth of 108 at his position with a 24.5 On-Off, is Out, and Fox is Day-To-Day. Stephon Castle has carried the most minutes, but the lineups with Harper and Fox together have been the best non-Wembanyama groups. How long Harper is out matters more than anything else on the injury list.

concerns.title: Three-point shooting at both ends
concerns.body: The Spurs hit just 33.7% from three (24th) while allowing 36.8% (also 24th). Both numbers are more likely to improve than hold over 17 games, since last year's team shot 35.9%. Still, a team that wins by suffocating the paint gives up threes, and a hot-shooting opponent is how it loses.

trend.note: October went 4-2 with a leaky 110.17 allowed a game. November tightened to 10-1 and 102.73 allowed, with a 12-game win streak. Over the last five games the defense allowed 6.35 fewer points a game than its season mark, even as scoring dipped.

weekAhead.headline: Two cupcakes bracket home tests against the Lakers and Boston
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with road trips to Sacramento and Portland, both teams the Spurs beat on the road earlier this month by comfortable margins. It closes at Milwaukee, which at 1-16 has the league's worst defense. In between come the real measuring sticks, both at home. The Lakers are also 14-3, with the league's best eFG %. Boston brings a third-ranked defense and a 9.5 Net Rtg.

The Boston game and the Milwaukee trip are on back-to-back nights, which is the main scheduling risk, especially with Wembanyama and Fox both Day-To-Day. A 4-1 week is the base case. Going 5-0 needs a win over either the Lakers or Boston, and a 3-2 week most likely means injuries cost them one of the soft games.

keyMatchups.title: Spurs glass versus Lakers' rebounding hole
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers shoot better than anyone, but they rebound only 68.8% of opponents' misses, 29th in the league. San Antonio's 28.6 ORB % should produce extra possessions. Those second chances offset a Lakers defense that forces turnovers at the league's highest rate. The Spurs' own low TOV % is the counter.

keyMatchups.title: Boston's center defense meets Wembanyama
keyMatchups.body: Boston holds centers 3.31 points under their usual output, best in the league. It also keeps opponents away from the rim at the third-lowest rate. Boston launches threes at the league's second-highest rate, aimed straight at the Spurs' 24th-ranked perimeter defense. This is the game most likely to go the other way.

keyMatchups.title: Soft interiors in Milwaukee and Portland
keyMatchups.body: Milwaukee lets centers exceed their usual PRA by 7.78, the most in the league, and Portland is also last in points allowed to centers against their averages. If Wembanyama plays, both games set up for a big night inside. The Portland trip has been comfortable once already this month.

weekAhead.watch: Wembanyama's status and minutes across the Boston–Milwaukee back-to-back.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable. The record matches the margin, the defense is built on rim protection rather than forced turnovers, and the ball security repeats last season's profile. Two numbers should move in the Spurs' favor: opponents' 36.8% from three and their own 33.7% both look like early-season noise against last year's baselines. The current pace of 68 wins is likely too high, though. Seventeen games of a league-best margin rarely hold for 82, and this team has little cushion behind its stars.

Expect something like 59 to 64 wins and a Net Rtg settling in the high single digits to low double digits. That keeps them at or near the top of the West. The swing case is health. With Wembanyama healthy, the Spurs are the best team in the league. Without him, the frontcourt's On-Off numbers say they are merely good, and the Harper absence will show how deep the A+ backcourt really is.

confidence.note: Seventeen games is a small sample, but the margin, defense and last year's 62-win season all point the same way; injuries cloud the outlook.
